projects.name: Mactung Tungsten Project — Feasibility Study & Mine Development
projects.description: Fireweed Metals has engaged engineering consultants for an updated feasibility study on the Mactung tungsten deposit on the Yukon-NWT border (41.5 Mt indicated at 0.73% WO3). U.S. Department of Defense awarded US$15.8M under the Defense Production Act; combined Canada-U.S. funding of up to $35M supports initial planning. Feasibility study targeted early 2027, final investment decision early 2028.

evidence.title: Fireweed advances Mactung toward mining
evidence.snippet: Fireweed Metals has engaged consultants to complete updated Feasibility Study for 100%-owned Mactung Tungsten Project in Yukon.

evidence.title: Mactung Project — Fireweed Metals
evidence.snippet: Mactung hosts 41.5 Mt indicated resource averaging 0.73% WO3 — among the largest high-grade tungsten deposits outside China.

projects.name: Sunrise Farms Woodstock Poultry Processing Plant
projects.description: Sunrise Farms is constructing a new 155,000-sq-ft poultry processing facility in Woodstock, Ontario. Ontario government providing $4M through Invest Ontario. Project creates 100 new jobs, supports 248 existing positions, scheduled completion end of 2027. Described by CEO as 'largest greenfield investment in Sunrise's history.'

evidence.title: Sunrise Farms to build $100M poultry processing plant in Woodstock, Ont.
evidence.snippet: Sunrise Farms is investing $100.5 million to construct a new 155,000 square foot, state of the art poultry processing facility in Woodstock.

evidence.title: Invest Ontario supports Sunrise Farms major expansion in Woodstock
evidence.snippet: Ontario government providing $4 million through Invest Ontario to support construction of the facility.

projects.name: Hilton Foods Canada Brantford Food Processing Facility
projects.description: Hilton Foods Canada is building a 230,000-sq-ft food processing and warehouse distribution facility in Brantford, Ontario — the company's first North American plant. Will process beef, pork, lamb, and seafood for distribution to Mississauga, Cornwall, and Moncton. Ontario government investing $1.5M from Southwestern Ontario Development Fund. Supports 150 jobs.

evidence.title: Hilton Foods to build $192M food processing facility in Brantford
evidence.snippet: Hilton Foods Canada is spending $192 million to build its first North American food processing and distribution facility in Brantford, Ont.

evidence.title: Hilton Foods begins construction on new plant in Canada facility
evidence.snippet: 230,000-square-foot food processing and warehouse distribution facility, processing protein products including beef, pork, lamb, and seafood.

projects.name: Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn — Hudson's Bay Building Adaptive Reuse
projects.description: Southern Chiefs' Organization is converting the 655,000-sq-ft former Hudson's Bay Company flagship building at Portage Avenue and Memorial Boulevard, Winnipeg, into Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn — a mixed-use development with 373 housing units, restaurants, offices and retail. Budget escalated from $130M (2022) to $200M (2023) to $310M (2026) due to inflation, supply chain pressures and heritage upgrade scope. Three levels of government have pledged $141M in cash, loans and tax relief.

evidence.title: Cost of redeveloping former Bay building in Winnipeg now $310M, Southern Chiefs says
evidence.snippet: SCO Grand Chief Jerry Daniels said the project will cost $310 million; project includes 373 housing units, restaurants, office and retail.

evidence.title: Cost of Winnipeg Bay store redevelopment jumps to $310-million
evidence.snippet: Three levels of government have pledged $141 million in cash, loans and tax relief to help SCO complete the project.

projects.name: Yondr Toronto Hyperscale Data Centre Campus
projects.description: Yondr's first Canadian data centre — a 27 MW facility broken ground in January 2025 on a 4.5-acre Toronto site. Total investment between CAD $2.5B and $4B. Backed with CAD $320M financing from Desjardins Group, Scotiabank, and Export Development Canada. Hydro One providing power infrastructure support.

evidence.title: Largest Upcoming Data Centers in Canada 2026
evidence.snippet: Yondr data center: 27 MW facility, 4.5-acre Toronto site, CAD 2.5B-4B investment, Yondr's first Canadian data center, CAD 320M financing from Desjardins, Scotiabank, EDC.

evidence.title: Stack launches Canadian data center in Toronto
evidence.snippet: Reference to Yondr Toronto facility breaking ground January 2025 as first Canadian site for the operator.

projects.name: Stack Infrastructure Toronto 56MW Data Centre Campus
projects.description: Stack Infrastructure delivered first 8MW phase of a 56MW data centre campus in Toronto, Ontario. Next 24MW phase planned for delivery in Q2 2026. Total campus capacity 56MW.

evidence.title: Stack launches Canadian data center in Toronto
evidence.snippet: Stack announced delivery of first 8MW phase of 56MW campus in Ontario, next 24MW phase planned Q2 2026.

projects.name: Bull Arm Floating Dry Dock — Newfoundland Marine Fabrication Expansion
projects.proponent: OilCo (Newfoundland and Labrador Crown corp); Equinor; BP
projects.description: Equinor and BP will contribute $200M to fabricate a large-scale (7,000-8,000 tonne) floating dry dock at Bull Arm, Trinity Bay — Atlantic Canada's largest fabrication site. Constructed by unionized TradesNL workers; owned by provincial crown OilCo. Tied to Bay du Nord life-of-field benefits agreement signed March 2026. Province will include funding in upcoming budget for initial planning phase.

evidence.title: Agreement to Advance Bay du Nord Project will Create Thousands of Jobs, Generate Billions in Revenue
evidence.snippet: $200 million in fabrication funds to facilitate long-term fabrication trades jobs, used to secure capital to build a large floating dry dock at Bull Arm.

evidence.title: N.L. reaches deal with Equinor, BP to open the way for construction, production of Bay du Nord
evidence.snippet: Floating dry dock at Bull Arm to be owned by OilCo, constructed by unionized TradesNL workers.

projects.name: Microsoft Azure Vaughan Data Centre Expansion
projects.description: Microsoft expanding Azure Canada Central data-centre region with new facility in Vaughan, Greater Toronto Area. Multi-billion-dollar investment expected to support 1,250 jobs. Microsoft has committed publicly that the new Ontario data centres will not increase power bills. Note: may overlap with existing Microsoft Azure Canada Central — York Region Data Centres entry; Vaughan site appears to be a distinct/expanded build.

evidence.title: Invest Ontario Welcomes Microsoft's Data Centre Expansion Plans
evidence.snippet: Microsoft will expand Azure Canada Central data-centre region in Ontario, expected to support 1,250 jobs, multi-billion-dollar investment in GTA, specifically in Vaughan.

evidence.title: Microsoft promises new Ontario data centres won't increase power bills
evidence.snippet: Microsoft Ontario data centres expansion in Vaughan area discussed in context of power and water use commitments.

projects.name: EverWind Nova Scotia Onshore Wind Portfolio — Phase 1
projects.proponent: EverWind Fuels; Membertou First Nation (majority); Paqtnkek First Nation; Potlotek First Nation; Nuveen Infrastructure Credit
projects.description: EverWind Fuels secured $240M (US$175M from Nuveen Infrastructure Credit) in March 2026 to construct first phase of four onshore wind farms in Nova Scotia that will power an associated green hydrogen and ammonia plant in Richmond County, Cape Breton. Phase one represents >$2B in capital investment. Construction to begin in 2026, first wind energy online 2028. Initial hydrogen plant phase 200,000 tonnes/year green ammonia. Indigenous consortium led by Membertou First Nation holds majority ownership.

evidence.title: American investment in EverWind to kick-start buildout of first 4 wind farms
evidence.snippet: EverWind Fuels secured $240-million in financing to construct onshore wind farms and associated green hydrogen project, first phase exceeding $2 billion.

evidence.title: EverWind Secures US$175 Million Strategic Investment from Nuveen
evidence.snippet: US$175M strategic investment from Nuveen to advance largest Atlantic Canadian clean energy platform.

projects.name: Vale-Exiro-Canada Growth Fund Thompson Nickel Operation Investment

projects.description: Partnership including Vale, Toronto-based Exiro Minerals, an American financing company, and the federal Canada Growth Fund plans to invest up to $280M in the Thompson, Manitoba nickel operation to keep the mine open with eyes on expansion after partial sale.

evidence.title: New partnership to keep Thompson mine open, eyes expansion after partial sale
evidence.snippet: Partnership including Vale, American financing company, Toronto-based Exiro Minerals and federal Canada Growth Fund plans to invest up to $280 million in Thompson nickel operation.

projects.name: CFB Esquimalt A and B Jetty Replacement

Project expected to support approximately 1,280 jobs during construction; delivers seismically resilient infrastructure on the Pacific Coast.

evidence.title: Government announces $1.1B for the Esquimalt jetty project
evidence.snippet: Government announced $1.1 billion to replace aging A and B jetties in Esquimalt, BC, supporting RCN operations; 1,280 jobs during construction.

projects.description: Federal government supporting 9 projects with more than $63M in funding for rural and northern Manitoba infrastructure. $61M+ will connect over 2,300 households in 11+ communities — including 2,100+ Indigenous households — to reliable, affordable high-speed internet. Announced May 15, 2026.

evidence.title: Vital infrastructure and connectivity supported across rural and northern Manitoba
evidence.snippet: Government of Canada supporting 9 projects with more than $63 million in funding for rural and northern communities in Manitoba; $61M+ for connectivity to 2,300+ households.
